code\n239\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n240\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n241\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n242\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n243\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n244\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n245\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n246\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n247\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n248\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n249\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n250\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n251\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n252\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n253\t        }\n254\t    }\n255\t\n256\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n257\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n258\t        match self {\n259\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n260\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n261\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n262\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n263\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n264\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n265\t        }\n266\t    }\n267\t}\n268\t\n269\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n270\t// DecompositionMode\n271\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n272\t\n273\t/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n274\t///\n275\t/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n276\t/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n277\t///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n278\t///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n279\t///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n280\t/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n281\t///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n282\t///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n283\t///   and consecutive failure count.\n284\t///\n285\t/// # When to use each mode\n286\t///\n287\t/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n288\t/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n289\t/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n290\t/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n291\t/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n292\t///\n293\t/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n294\t/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n295\t/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n296\t/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n297\t/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n298\t///\n299\t/// # API boundary\n300\t///\n301\t/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n302\t/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n303\t/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n304\t#[non_exhaustive]\n305\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n306\t#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n307\tpub enum DecompositionMode {\n308\t    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n309\t    ///\n310\t    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n311\t    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n312\t    Timeout {\n313\t        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n314\t        timeout_seconds: u64,\n315\t        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n316\t        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n317\t        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n318\t    },\n319\t    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n320\t    ///\n321\t    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n322\t    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n323\t    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n324\t    OrdinaryFailure,\n325\t}\n326\t\n327\timpl DecompositionMode {\n328\t    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n329\t    ///\n330\t    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n331\t    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n332\t    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n333\t    ///\n334\t    /// # Examples\n335\t    ///\n336\t    /// ```\n337\t    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n338\t    ///\n339\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n340\t    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n341\t    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n342\t    /// };\n343\t    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n344\t    ///\n345\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n346\t    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n347\t    /// ```\n348\t    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n349\t        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n350\t    }\n351\t\n352\t    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n353\t    ///\n354\t    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n355\t    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n356\t    ///\n357\t    /// # Examples\n358\t    ///\n359\t    /// ```\n360\t    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n361\t    ///\n362\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n363\t    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n364\t    ///\n365\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n366\t    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n367\t    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n368\t    /// };\n369\t    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n370\t    /// ```\n371\t    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n372\t        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n373\t    }\n374\t\n375\t    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n376\t    ///\n377\t    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n378\t    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n379\t    ///\n380\t    /// # Examples\n381\t    ///\n382\t    /// ```\n383\t    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n384\t    ///\n385\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n386\t    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n387\t    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n388\t    /// };\n389\t    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n390\t    ///\n391\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n392\t    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n393\t    /// ```\n394\t    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n395\t        match self {\n396\t            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n397\t                timeout_seconds, ..\n398\t            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n399\t            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n400\t        }\n401\t    }\n402\t\n403\t    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n404\t    ///\n405\t    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n406\t    /// without pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode\n407\t    /// or when the hint is not set.\n408\t    ///\n409\t    /// # Examples\n410\t    ///\n411\t    /// ```\n412\t    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n413\t    ///\n414\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n415\t    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n416\t    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n417\t    /// };\n418\t    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), Some(&\"Phase 1\".to_string()));\n419\t    ///\n420\t    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n421\t    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n422\t    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n423\t    /// };\n424\t    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), None);\n425\t    /// ```\n426\t    pub fn current_phase_hint(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n427\t        match self {\n428\t            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n429\t                current_phase_hint, ..\n430\t            } => current_phase_hint.as_ref(),\n431\t            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n432\t        }\n433\t    }\n434\t}\n435\t\n436\timpl fmt::Display for DecompositionMode {\n437\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n438\t        match self {\n439\t            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n440\t                timeout_seconds, ..\n441\t            } => write!(f, \"timeout ({}s)\", timeout_seconds),\n442\t            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => write!(f, \"ordinary_failure\"),\n443\t        }\n444\t    }\n445\t}\n446\t\n447\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n448\t// DecompositionDecision\n449\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n450\t\n451\t/// Decision whether to decompose a bead into child beads or refuse decomposition.\n452\t///\n453\t/// This enum represents the outcome of evaluating whether a bead should be split\n454\t/// into smaller child beads after repeated timeout failures. The decision is based\n455\t/// on timeout thresholds, retry counts, and bead characteristics.\n456\t#[non_exhaustive]\n457\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n458\tpub enum DecompositionDecision {\n459\t    /// The bead should be split into the proposed child beads.\n460\t    ///\n461\t    /// Contains the vector of child bead proposals that will be created.\n462\t    Split { proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal> },\n463\t    /// The bead should not be decomposed.\n464\t    ///\n465\t    /// Contains a human-readable reason explaining why decomposition was refused.\n466\t    Refuse { reason: String },\n467\t}\n468\t\n469\timpl DecompositionDecision {\n470\t    /// Evaluate whether a bead should be decomposed based on its characteristics.\n471\t    ///\n472\t    /// This function implements the decision tree for timeout-driven decomposition:\n473\t    ///\n474\t    /// # Decision Tree\n475\t    ///\n476\t    /// 1. **Check timeout threshold**: Returns `Refuse` if timeout is below minimum threshold\n477\t    /// 2. **Check retry count**: Returns `Refuse` if retry count is below minimum limit\n478\t    /// 3. **Check bead size**: Returns `Refuse` if bead is too small (body < threshold chars)\n479\t    /// 4. **Check active assignee**: Returns `Refuse` if bead has an active assignee\n480\t    /// 5. **Check if already a child**: Returns `Refuse` if bead is already a child bead\n481\t    /// 6. **All checks pass**: Returns `Split` with the provided proposals\n482\t    ///\n483\t    /// # Arguments\n484\t    ///\n485\t    /// * `timeout_seconds` - The timeout duration that was exceeded\n486\t    /// * `retry_count` - Number of consecutive timeout failures\n487\t    /// * `bead_body` - Optional bead body text for size check\n488\t    /// * `has_assignee` - Whether the bead currently has an assignee\n489\t    /// * `is_child_bead` - Whether the bead is already a child (has mitosis-child label)\n490\t    /// * `proposals` - Child bead proposals to use if decision is `Split`\n491\t    /// * `config` - Optional configuration overrides (uses defaults if None)\n492\t    ///\n493\t    /// # Returns\n494\t    ///\n495\t    /// * `Split { proposals }` if all checks pass\n496\t    /// * `Refuse { reason }` if any check fails\n497\t    ///\n498\t    /// # Examples\n499\t    ///\n500\t    /// ```\n501\t    /// use needle::types::{DecompositionDecision, ChildBeadProposal, BeadId};\n502\t    ///\n503\t    /// let proposals = vec![\n504\t    ///     ChildBeadProposal::new(\n505\t    ///         \"Phase 1\".to_string(),\n506\t    ///         \"Description\".to_string(),\n507\t    ///         vec![BeadId::from(\"needle-parent\")],\n508\t    ///         2,\n509\t    ///     ).unwrap(),\n510\t    /// ];\n511\t    ///\n512\t    /// // High   proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal>,\n543\t        config: Option<DecompositionConfig>,\n544\t    ) -> Self {\n545\t        let config = config.unwrap_or_default();\n546\t\n547\t        // Check 1: Timeout threshold\n548\t        if timeout_seconds < config.min_timeout_threshold {\n549\t            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n550\t                reason: format!(\n551\t                    \"timeout ({}) is below minimum threshold ({}s)\",\n552\t                    timeout_seconds, config.min_timeout_threshold\n553\t                ),\n554\t            };\n555\t        }\n556\t\n557\t        // Check 2: Retry count\n558\t        if retry_count < config.min_retry_limit {\n559\t            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n560\t                reason: format!(\n561\t                    \"retry count ({}) is below minimum limit ({})\",\n562\t                    retry_count, config.min_retry_limit\n563\t                ),\n564\t            };\n565\t        }\n566\t\n567\t        // Check 3: Bead size (if body is available)\n568\t        if let Some(body) = bead_body {\n569\t            if body.len() < config.min_bead_size_chars {\n570\t                return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n571\t                    reason: format!(\n572\t                        \"bead body ({} chars) is too small for decomposition (minimum: {} chars)\",\n573\t                        body.len(), config.min_bead_size_chars\n574\t                    ),\n575\t                };\n576\t            }\n577\t        }\n578\t\n579\t        // Check 4: Active assignee\n580\t        if has_assignee {\n581\t            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n582\t                reason: \"bead has an active assignee\".to_string(),\n583\t            };\n584\t        }\n585\t\n586\t        // Check 5: Already a child bead\n587\t        if is_child_bead {\n588\t            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n589\t                reason: \"bead is already a child bead (has mitosis-child label)\".to_string(),\n590\t            };\n591\t        }\n592\t\n593\t        // All checks passed - approve the split\n594\t        DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals }\n595\t    }\n596\t\n597\t    /// Returns true if this decision approves splitting.\n598\t    pub fn is_split(&self) -> bool {\n599\t        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Split { .. })\n600\t    }\n601\t\n602\t    /// Returns true if this decision refuses decomposition.\n603\t    pub fn is_refuse(&self) -> bool {\n604\t        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. })\n605\t    }\n606\t\n607\t    /// Get the refusal reason if this is a `Refuse` decision.\n608\t    pub fn refusal_reason(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n609\t        match self {\n610\t            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => Some(reason),\n611\t            _ => None,\n612\t        }\n613\t    }\n614\t\n615\t    /// Get the child proposals if this is a `Split` decision.\n616\t }\n637\t}\n638\t\n639\t/// Configuration thresholds for decomposition decisions.\n640\t///\n641\t/// These thresholds control when a bead qualifies for timeout-driven decomposition.\n642\t/// Default Every variant must be explicitly handled at every call site.\n\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::ops::Deref;\nuse std::str::FromStr;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BeadId newtype\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A validated bead identifier (e.g., `needle-gob`).\n///\n/// Wraps `String` with `Display`, `FromStr`, `Hash`, and `Eq` impls.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(transparent)]\npub struct BeadId(String);\n\nimpl fmt::Display for BeadId {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        f.write_str(&self.0)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromStr for BeadId {\n    type Err = std::convert::Infallible;\n\n    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {\n        Ok(BeadId(s.to_owned()))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<String> for BeadId {\n    fn from(s: String) -> Self {\n        BeadId(s)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<&str> for BeadId {\n    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {\n        BeadId(s.to_owned())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<BeadId> for String {\n    fn from(id: BeadId) -> Self {\n        id.0\n    }\n}\n\nimpl AsRef<str> for BeadId {\n    fn as_ref(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.0\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Deref for BeadId {\n    type Target = str;\n\n    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {\n        &self.0\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// WorkerId type alias\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Identifies a worker instance (e.g., `needle-01`).\npub type WorkerId = String;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Priority type alias\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Priority level of a bead. Lower number = higher priority (P1 > P2 > P3).\npub type Priority = u8;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BeadStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Lifecycle status of a bead in the store.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum BeadStatus {\n    Open,\n    InProgress,\n    /// `bf` (bead-forge) has been observed emitting `\"completed\"` for done\n    /// beads on some workspaces (bf's own `Status` enum has no `Completed`\n    /// variant — it falls through to an untagged `Custom(String)`, so this\n    /// slips through bf-side validation). Accept it as an alias so a single\n    /// such bead doesn't fail `bf list --json` deserialization for every\n    /// other bead in the same call — see needle-weave-completed-status.\n    #[serde(alias = \"completed\")]\n    Done,\n    /// `br show --json` emits `\"closed\"` for done beads. Treat as equivalent\n    /// to `Done` so deserialization succeeds.\n    Closed,\n    Blocked,\n    /// `bf` (bead-forge) emits `\"deferred\"` for beads deliberately postponed\n    /// rather than blocked by a dependency. Distinct from `Blocked`: a\n    /// deferred bead has no unmet dependency, it was just set aside — see\n    /// GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#10. Without this variant, `bf list --json`\n    /// fails deserialization for every such bead, and it silently disappears\n    /// from strand/supervise visibility with no surfaced error.\n    Deferred,\n}\n\nimpl BeadStatus {\n    /// Returns true if the bead is finished (either `Done` or `Closed`).\n    pub fn is_done(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, BeadStatus::Done | BeadStatus::Closed)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for BeadStatus {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            BeadStatus::Open => write!(f, \"open\"),\n            BeadStatus::InProgress => write!(f, \"in_progress\"),\n            BeadStatus::Done | BeadStatus::Closed => write!(f, \"done\"),\n            BeadStatus::Blocked => write!(f, \"blocked\"),\n            BeadStatus::Deferred => write!(f, \"deferred\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// WorkerState\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Worker finite-state-machine states.\n///\n/// Every state has defined entry conditions, actions, and exit transitions.\n/// There are no implicit states or fallthrough paths.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE\")]\npub enum WorkerState {\n    Booting,\n    Selecting,\n    Claiming,\n    Retrying,\n    Building,\n    Dispatching,\n    Executing,\n    Handling,\n    Logging,\n    /// All strands returned empty — worker has nothing to do.\n    Exhausted,\n    /// Received graceful shutdown signal.\n    Stopped,\n    /// Unrecoverable error.\n    Errored,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for WorkerState {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        let s = match self {\n            WorkerState::Booting => \"BOOTING\",\n            WorkerState::Selecting => \"SELECTING\",\n            WorkerState::Claiming => \"CLAIMING\",\n            WorkerState::Retrying => \"RETRYING\",\n            WorkerState::Building => \"BUILDING\",\n            WorkerState::Dispatching => \"DISPATCHING\",\n            WorkerState::Executing => \"EXECUTING\",\n            WorkerState::Handling => \"HANDLING\",\n            WorkerState::Logging => \"LOGGING\",\n            WorkerState::Exhausted => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            WorkerState::Stopped => \"STOPPED\",\n            WorkerState::Errored => \"ERRORED\",\n        };\n        f.write_str(s)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Outcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n///\n/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n    Failure,\n    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n    AgentNotFound,\n    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n    Interrupted,\n    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n    Crash(i32),\n}\n\nimpl Outcome {\n    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n    ///\n    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum DecompositionMode {\n    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n    Timeout {\n        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n    OrdinaryFailure,\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionMode {\n    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n    /// without pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode\n    /// or when the hint is not set.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), Some(&\"Phase 1\".to_string()));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn current_phase_hint(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                current_phase_hint, ..\n            } => current_phase_hint.as_ref(),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionMode {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => write!(f, \"timeout ({}s)\", timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => write!(f, \"ordinary_failure\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionDecision\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Decision whether to decompose a bead into child beads or refuse decomposition.\n///\n/// This enum represents the outcome of evaluating whether a bead should be split\n/// into smaller child beads after repeated timeout failures. The decision is based\n/// on timeout thresholds, retry counts, and bead characteristics.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DecompositionDecision {\n    /// The bead should be split into the proposed child beads.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the vector of child bead proposals that will be created.\n    Split { proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal> },\n    /// The bead should not be decomposed.\n    ///\n    /// Contains a human-readable reason explaining why decomposition was refused.\n    Refuse { reason: String },\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionDecision {\n    /// Evaluate whether a bead should be decomposed based on its characteristics.\n    ///\n    /// This function implements the decision tree for timeout-driven decomposition:\n    ///\n    /// # Decision Tree\n    ///\n    /// 1. **Check timeout threshold**: Returns `Refuse` if timeout is below minimum threshold\n    /// 2. **Check retry count**: Returns `Refuse` if retry count is below minimum limit\n    /// 3. **Check bead size**: Returns `Refuse` if bead is too small (body < threshold chars)\n    /// 4. **Check active assignee**: Returns `Refuse` if bead has an active assignee\n    /// 5. **Check if already a child**: Returns `Refuse` if bead is already a child bead\n    /// 6. **All checks pass**: Returns `Split` with the provided proposals\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `timeout_seconds` - The timeout duration that was exceeded\n    /// * `retry_count` - Number of consecutive timeout failures\n    /// * `bead_body` - Optional bead body text for size check\n    /// * `has_assignee` - Whether the bead currently has an assignee\n    /// * `is_child_bead` - Whether the bead is already a child (has mitosis-child label)\n    /// * `proposals` - Child bead proposals to use if decision is `Split`\n    /// * `config` - Optional configuration overrides (uses defaults if None)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// * `Split { proposals }` if all checks pass\n    /// * `Refuse { reason }` if any check fails\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::{DecompositionDecision, ChildBeadProposal, BeadId};\n    ///\n    /// let proposals = vec![\n    ///     ChildBeadProposal::new(\n    ///         \"Phase 1\".to_string(),\n    ///         \"Description\".to_string(),\n    ///         vec![BeadId::from(\"needle-parent\")],\n    ///         2,\n    ///     ).unwrap(),\n    /// ];\n    ///\n    /// // High timeout, many retries, no assignee -> should split\n    /// let decision = DecompositionDecision::evaluate(\n    ///     300,      // 5 minute timeout\n    ///     3,        // 3 retries\n    ///     Some(&\"Large bead body\".to_string()),\n    ///     false,    // no assignee\n    ///     false,    // not a child\n    ///     proposals.clone(),\n    ///     None,\n    /// );\n    /// assert!(matches!(decision, DecompositionDecision::Split { .. }));\n    ///\n    /// // Low timeout -> should refuse\n    /// let decision = DecompositionDecision::evaluate(\n    ///     30,       // 30 second timeout\n    ///     3,\n    ///     Some(&\"Large bead body\".to_string()),\n    ///     false,\n    ///     false,\n    ///     proposals,\n    ///     None,\n    /// );\n    /// assert!(matches!(decision, DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. }));\n    /// ```\n    pub fn evaluate(\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        retry_count: u32,\n        bead_body: Option<&String>,\n        has_assignee: bool,\n        is_child_bead: bool,\n        proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal>,\n        config: Option<DecompositionConfig>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let config = config.unwrap_or_default();\n\n        // Check 1: Timeout threshold\n        if timeout_seconds < config.min_timeout_threshold {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: format!(\n                    \"timeout ({}) is below minimum threshold ({}s)\",\n                    timeout_seconds, config.min_timeout_threshold\n                ),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Check 2: Retry count\n        if retry_count < config.min_retry_limit {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: format!(\n                    \"retry count ({}) is below minimum limit ({})\",\n                    retry_count, config.min_retry_limit\n                ),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Check 3: Bead size (if body is available)\n        if let Some(body) = bead_body {\n            if body.len() < config.min_bead_size_chars {\n                return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                    reason: format!(\n                        \"bead body ({} chars) is too small for decomposition (minimum: {} chars)\",\n                        body.len(), config.min_bead_size_chars\n                    ),\n                };\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check 4: Active assignee\n        if has_assignee {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: \"bead has an active assignee\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Check 5: Already a child bead\n        if is_child_bead {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: \"bead is already a child bead (has mitosis-child label)\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // All checks passed - approve the split\n        DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this decision approves splitting.\n    pub fn is_split(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Split { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this decision refuses decomposition.\n    pub fn is_refuse(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the refusal reason if this is a `Refuse` decision.\n    pub fn refusal_reason(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => Some(reason),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the child proposals if this is a `Split` decision.\n    pub fn proposals(&self) -> Option<&Vec<ChildBeadProposal>> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals } => Some(proposals),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"split into {} child bead(s)\",\n                proposals.len()\n            ),\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => {\n                write!(f, \"refuse decomposition: {}\", reason)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Configuration thresholds for decomposition decisions.\n///\n/// These thresholds control when a bead qualifies for timeout-driven decomposition.\n/// Default values are chosen to balance between:\n/// - Avoiding premature decomposition of beads that might succeed on retry\n/// - Decomposing beads that are genuinely too large to complete in one attempt\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DecompositionConfig {\n    /// Minimum timeout duration (in seconds) to qualify for decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Beads that timeout in less time are assumed to have failed for reasons\n    /// other than size (e.g., compilation errors, deadlocks, network issues).\n    /// Default: 120 seconds (2 minutes).\n    pub min_timeout_threshold: u64,\n\n    /// Minimum number of consecutive timeout failures before decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// This prevents decomposition on the first timeout, giving the bead a chance\n    /// to succeed on retry (e.g., transient issues, resource contention).\n    /// Default: 2 retries.\n    pub min_retry_limit: u32,\n\n    /// Minimum bead body size (in characters) to qualify for decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Very small beads don't benefit from splitting - they're either quick fixes\n    /// or genuinely broken. Default: 200 characters.\n    pub min_bead_size_chars: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for DecompositionConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        DecompositionConfig {\n            min_timeout_threshold: 120,  // 2 minutes\n            min_retry_limit: 2,          // 2 consecutive timeouts\n            min_bead_size_chars: 200,    // 200 characters\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). `Skipped` means \"did not\n    /// run because the environment doesn't support it\" — e.g., a strand that\n    /// requires a home bead store when the worker is configured without one.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"truly no candidates\").\n    /// `FoundButExcluded` means \"candidates exist but this worker can't claim\n    /// them right now\" — they're assigned to other workers or blocked by labels.\n    /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// Claim CLI failed with a store/CLI error (distinct from race-lost).\n    ClaimError {\n        /// Human-readable error message.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br`/`bf` JSON output, or from\n/// bead-rs's `bead` (`{\"blocker\": \"<id>\", \"kind\": \"blocks\"}` — a lean\n/// edge-only shape with no enriched title/status/priority). The aliases\n/// below accept both without changing how bf/br JSON deserializes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BrDependency {\n    #[serde(alias = \"blocker\")]\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub title: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub status: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    #[serde(rename = \"dependency_type\", alias = \"kind\", default)]\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A comment on a bead.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Comment {\n    /// Comment ID (internal database ID).\n    pub id: i64,\n    /// The bead this comment is on.\n    #[serde(rename = \"issue_id\")]\n    pub bead_id: String,\n    /// The comment text.\n    pub text: String,\n    /// Author who created the comment.\n    pub author: String,\n    /// When the comment was created.\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n/// A bead as returned from the bead store.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Bead {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Stored as `description` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"description\")]\n    pub body: Option<String>,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub status: BeadStatus,\n    /// br emits `\"\"` for unassigned beads; normalize to `None`.\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"empty_string_as_none\")]\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// br may omit this field when empty.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Stored as `source_repo` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"source_repo\", default)]\n    pub workspace: std::path::PathBuf,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependents: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    /// Comments on this bead, returned by `bf show --json`.\n    /// Empty array if no comments or backend doesn't support comments.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub comments: Vec<Comment>,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    // br ready --json omits updated_at; default to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// InputMethod\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How the prompt is passed to the agent binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"method\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum InputMethod {\n    /// Write the prompt to the agent's stdin.\n    Stdin,\n    /// Write the prompt to a temp file and pass the path.\n    File {\n        /// Template for the temp file path. `{bead_id}` is substituted.\n        path_template: String,\n    },\n    /// Pass the prompt as a CLI argument.\n    Args {\n        /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Path reference to a worker's heartbeat file on disk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HeartbeatFile {\n    pub path: std::path::PathBuf,\n}\n\n/// Health status of a peer worker as inferred from its heartbeat file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum PeerStatus {\n    /// Heartbeat is fresh — peer is considered alive.\n    Alive {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        current_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat TTL has elapsed — peer may be stuck.\n    Stale {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        claimed_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat file is missing — peer is dead or never started.\n    Dead { heartbeat_file: HeartbeatFile },\n}\n\n// assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-1, false), Outcome::Crash(-1));\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-9, false), Outcome::Crash(-9));\n        // Large positive values >255 -> Crash per spec (exit > `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum DecompositionMode {\n    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n    Timeout {\n        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n    OrdinaryFailure,\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionMode {\n    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n    /// without pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode\n    /// or when the hint is not set.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), Some(&\"Phase 1\".to_string()));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn current_phase_hint(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                current_phase_hint, ..\n            } => current_phase_hint.as_ref(),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionMode {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => write!(f, \"timeout ({}s)\", timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => write!(f, \"ordinary_failure\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionDecision\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Decision whether to decompose a bead into child beads or refuse decomposition.\n///\n/// This enum represents the outcome of evaluating whether a bead should be split\n/// into smaller child beads after repeated timeout failures. The decision is based\n/// on timeout thresholds, retry counts, and bead characteristics.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DecompositionDecision {\n    /// The bead should be split into the proposed child beads.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the vector of child bead proposals that will be created.\n    Split { proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal> },\n    /// The bead should not be decomposed.\n    ///\n    /// Contains a human-readable reason explaining why decomposition was refused.\n    Refuse { reason: String },\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionDecision {\n    /// Evaluate whether a bead should be decomposed based on its characteristics.\n    ///\n    /// This function implements the decision tree for timeout-driven decomposition:\n    ///\n    /// # Decision Tree\n    ///\n    /// 1. **Check timeout threshold**: Returns `Refuse` if timeout is below minimum threshold\n    /// 2. **Check retry count**: Returns `Refuse` if retry count is below minimum limit\n    /// 3. **Check bead size**: Returns `Refuse` if bead is too small (body < threshold chars)\n    /// 4. **Check active assignee**: Returns `Refuse` if bead has an active assignee\n    /// 5. **Check if already a child**: Returns `Refuse` if bead is already a child bead\n    /// 6. **All checks pass**: Returns `Split` with the provided proposals\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `timeout_seconds` - The timeout duration that was exceeded\n    /// * `retry_count` - Number of consecutive timeout failures\n    /// * `bead_body` - Optional bead body text for size check\n    /// * `has_assignee` - Whether the bead currently has an assignee\n    /// * `is_child_bead` - Whether the bead is already a child (has mitosis-child label)\n    /// * `proposals` - Child bead proposals to use if decision is `Split`\n    /// * `config` - Optional configuration overrides (uses defaults if None)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// * `Split { proposals }` if all checks pass\n    /// * `Refuse { reason }` if any check fails\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::{DecompositionDecision, ChildBeadProposal, BeadId};\n    ///\n    /// let proposals = vec![\n    ///     ChildBeadProposal::new(\n    ///         \"Phase 1\".to_string(),\n    ///         \"Description\".to_string(),\n    ///         vec![BeadId::from(\"needle-parent\")],\n    ///         2,\n    ///     ).unwrap(),\n    /// ];\n    ///\n    /// // High timeout, many retries, no assignee -> should split\n    /// let decision = DecompositionDecision::evaluate(\n    ///     300,      // 5 minute timeout\n    ///     3,        // 3 retries\n    ///     Some(&\"Large bead body\".to_string()),\n    ///     false,    // no assignee\n    ///     false,    // not a child\n    ///     proposals.clone(),\n    ///     None,\n    /// );\n    /// assert!(matches!(decision, DecompositionDecision::Split { .. }));\n    ///\n    /// // Low timeout -> should refuse\n    /// let decision = DecompositionDecision::evaluate(\n    ///     30,       // 30 second timeout\n    ///     3,\n    ///     Some(&\"Large bead body\".to_string()),\n    ///     false,\n    ///     false,\n    ///     proposals,\n    ///     None,\n    /// );\n    /// assert!(matches!(decision, DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. }));\n    /// ```\n    pub fn evaluate(\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        retry_count: u32,\n        bead_body: Option<&String>,\n        has_assignee: bool,\n        is_child_bead: bool,\n        proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal>,\n        config: Option<DecompositionConfig>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let config = config.unwrap_or_default();\n\n        // Check 1: Timeout threshold\n        if timeout_seconds < config.min_timeout_threshold {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: format!(\n                    \"timeout ({}) is below minimum threshold ({}s)\",\n                    timeout_seconds, config.min_timeout_threshold\n                ),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Check 2: Retry count\n        if retry_count < config.min_retry_limit {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: format!(\n                    \"retry count ({}) is below minimum limit ({})\",\n                    retry_count, config.min_retry_limit\n                ),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Check 3: Bead size (if body is available)\n        if let Some(body) = bead_body {\n            if body.len() < config.min_bead_size_chars {\n                return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                    reason: format!(\n                        \"bead body ({} chars) is too small for decomposition (minimum: {} chars)\",\n                        body.len(), config.min_bead_size_chars\n                    ),\n                };\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check 4: Active assignee\n        if has_assignee {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: \"bead has an active assignee\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Check 5: Already a child bead\n        if is_child_bead {\n            return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n                reason: \"bead is already a child bead (has mitosis-child label)\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // All checks passed - approve the split\n        DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this decision approves splitting.\n    pub fn is_split(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Split { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this decision refuses decomposition.\n    pub fn is_refuse(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the refusal reason if this is a `Refuse` decision.\n    pub fn refusal_reason(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => Some(reason),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the child proposals if this is a `Split` decision.\n    pub fn proposals(&self) -> Option<&Vec<ChildBeadProposal>> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals } => Some(proposals),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { proposals } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"split into {} child bead(s)\",\n                proposals.len()\n            ),\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => {\n                write!(f, \"refuse decomposition: {}\", reason)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Configuration thresholds for decomposition decisions.\n///\n/// These thresholds control when a bead qualifies for timeout-driven decomposition.\n/// Default values are chosen to balance between:\n/// - Avoiding premature decomposition of beads that might succeed on retry\n/// - Decomposing beads that are genuinely too large to complete in one attempt\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DecompositionConfig {\n    /// Minimum timeout duration (in seconds) to qualify for decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Beads that timeout in less time are assumed to have failed for reasons\n    /// other than size (e.g., compilation errors, deadlocks, network issues).\n    /// Default: 120 seconds (2 minutes).\n    pub min_timeout_threshold: u64,\n\n    /// Minimum number of consecutive timeout failures before decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// This prevents decomposition on the first timeout, giving the bead a chance\n    /// to succeed on retry (e.g., transient issues, resource contention).\n    /// Default: 2 retries.\n    pub min_retry_limit: u32,\n\n    /// Minimum bead body size (in characters) to qualify for decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Very small beads don't benefit from splitting - they're either quick fixes\n    /// or genuinely broken. Default: 200 characters.\n    pub min_bead_size_chars: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for DecompositionConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        DecompositionConfig {\n            min_timeout_threshold: 120,  // 2 minutes\n            min_retry_limit: 2,          // 2 consecutive timeouts\n            min_bead_size_chars: 200,    // 200 characters\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand  /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n//      /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Path reference to a worker's heartbeat file on disk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HeartbeatFile {\n    pub path: std::path::PathBuf,\n}\n\n/// Health status of a peer worker as inferred from its heartbeat file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum PeerStatus {\n    /// Heartbeat is fresh — peer is considered alive.\n    Alive {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        current_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat TTL has elapsed — peer may be stuck.\n    Stale {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        claimed_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat file is missing — peer is dead or never started.\n    Dead { heartbeat_file: HeartbeatFile },\n}\n\n//     let s: String = id.clone().into();\n        assert_eq!(s, \"needle-gob\");\n        // From<&str>\n        let id2 = BeadId::from(\"needle-gob\");\n        assert_eq!(id, id2);\n        // Deref\n false), Outcome::Failure);\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(50, false), Outcome::Failure);\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(99, false), Outcome::Failure);\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(100, false), Outcome::Failure); // NOT timeout per spec\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(123, false), Outcome::Failure);\n        // 125-126 -> Failure (not AgentNotFound per spec)\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(125, false), Outcome::Failure);\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(126, false), Outcome::Failure);\n        // >128 -> Crash (signal exits)\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(128, false), Outcome::Failure); // 128 is NOT >128 per spec\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(129, false), Outcome::Crash(129));\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(130, false), Outcome::Crash(130)); // SIGINT -> Crash\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(137, false), Outcome::Crash(137)); // SIGKILL\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(143, false), Outcome::Crash(143)); // SIGTERM -> Crash\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(255, false), Outcome::Crash(255));\n        // negative -> Crash\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-1, false), Outcome::Crash(-1));\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-9, false), Outcome::Crash(-9));\n        // Large positive values >255 -> Crash per spec (exit > 128)\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(256, false), Outcome::Crash(256));\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(1000, false), Outcome::Crash(1000));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn
